'''Hélène Esnault''' (born 17 July 1953) is a French and German mathematician, specializing in [[algebraic geometry]].

==Career==
Born in Paris, Esnault earned her PhD in 1976 from the [[Paris Diderot University|University of Paris VII]]. She wrote her dissertation on ''Singularites rationnelles et groupes algebriques'' (Rational singularities and algebraic groups) under the direction of [[Lê Dũng Tráng]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=68523}}</ref><ref>{{OCLC|493820161}}</ref>

She did her habilitation at the [[University of Bonn]] in 1985, and pursued her studies at the [[University of Duisburg-Essen]]. Afterwards, she was a Heisenberg scholar of the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) at the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]] in Bonn.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.uni-due.de/en/research_leibnitz_award.php#EsnVie|title=Leibniz Award winner of the University of Duisburg-Essen|website=uni-due.de|access-date=2019-11-06}}</ref>

She became the first Einstein Professor at [[Freie Universität Berlin]] in 2012, as head of the algebra and number theory research group, after working previously at the University of Duisburg-Essen, the Max-Planck-Institut für Mathematik in Bonn, and at the University of Paris VII.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mi.fu-berlin.de/users/esnault/CV_ln2607.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|last=Esnault|first=Hélène|access-date=2018-12-29}}</ref>

In 2007 Esnault was a founding editor of the journal [[Algebra & Number Theory]]. From 1998 to 2010 she co-edited [[Mathematische Annalen]]; she has also served as editor of Acta Mathematica Vietnamica, [[Astérisque]], [[Duke Mathematical Journal]],  Mathematical Research Letters, [[Acta Mathematica]].

== Awards and honors ==
In 2001 she won the [[Prix Paul Doistau-Émile Blutet]] of the  [[Académie des sciences (France)|Académie des sciences]]<ref>[https://www.irphe.fr/~ansel/acad_2001.pdf Laureat]</ref>.
In 2003, she received together with [[Eckart Viehweg]] the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]].<ref>{https://www.dfg.de/de/gefoerderte-projekte/preistraeger-innen/leibniz-preis/2003}</ref>.
In 2019, she won the [[Cantor medal]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://idw-online.de/de/news706527|title=Cantor-Medaille 2019 für die Mathematikerin Hélène Esnault|website=idw-online.de|accessdate=16 December 2021}}</ref>.

In 2014 she was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]]<ref>{{citation|title=Member profile: Hélène Esnault|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/User/Esnault_H%C3%A9l%C3%A8ne|publisher=[[Academia Europaea]]|accessdate=2015-09-22}}</ref> and is a member of the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]], the [[Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities]]<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.bbaw.de/die-akademie/bbaw-mitglieder/mitglied-helene-esnault|title=Hélène Esnault|publisher=Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities}}</ref>, the {{ill|Europäische Akademie Nordrhein-Westfalen|de}}, the [[Danish Academy]]<ref>{
https://royalacademy.dk/new-members-elected-for-the-royal-danish-academy-of-sciences-and-letters/?lang=en}</ref>, the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Acad_Main/News/News2/MAEs%20elected%20Foreign%20Members%20of%20the%20Polish%20Academy%20of%20Sciences}</ref>.  

She received a Dr. Honoris Causa of the Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology
in 2009,  
of the  l'University of Rennes 
[[Université de Rennes]]
in 2013, of the  l'[[University of Chicago]] 
en 2023 <ref>{https://mathematics.uchicago.edu/news/article/honorary-doctorates-to-be-given-to-bob-zimmer-and-helene-esnault/}</ref>.

In 2026 she was awarded the [[Legion of Honour]].<ref>{https://jorfsearch.steinertriples.ch/name/Hélène%20Esnault}</ref>.
